items.title: Pool Closed for Repairs
items.text: Notice from Lakeside Community Pool. Because the heating system needs repair, the pool will be closed from Monday, November 2, to Friday, November 6. During this time, swimming lessons for children will move to the Hillview Sports Hall, which has a smaller pool. Lessons will start at 5:00 p.m., thirty minutes later than usual. Adult lap swimming will not be offered that week, but members may use the gym free of charge. We understand that the closure is inconvenient for many families, and we sincerely apologize. The pool will reopen on Saturday, November 7, at 8:00 a.m. with a free open-swim hour for all members. If you have any questions, please ask at the front desk or call the office between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.

qs.q: Where will children's swimming lessons be held during the closure?
o: In the Lakeside gym
At a school pool nearby
At the Hillview Sports Hall
In the smaller Lakeside pool
qs.why: 공지에 lessons for children will move to the Hillview Sports Hall이라고 나와 있어요.

qs.q: Which is most likely true about the repair work?
o: It will probably continue until the end of the month.
It was completed before this notice came out.
It is expected to be finished within a week.
It will only take place during the weekends.
qs.why: 월요일부터 금요일까지 닫고 토요일에 다시 연다고 했으므로 일주일 안에 끝날 것으로 예상할 수 있어요.

qs.q: How does the writer feel about the closure?
o: Happy about the chance to change things
Unconcerned about the families
Angry with the members
Sorry for the trouble it causes
qs.why: we sincerely apologize라는 표현에서 불편을 끼쳐 미안해하는 태도를 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "inconvenient" is closest in meaning to
o: costing a lot
causing difficulty
hard to understand
happening suddenly
qs.why: inconvenient는 '불편한', 즉 어려움이나 번거로움을 주는 것을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The opening of a new sports hall for local families
Rules for using the gym during the week
A price rise for pool members next month
A temporary closure and the changes it brings
qs.why: 수리 때문에 수영장이 잠시 닫히고 강습과 이용 방법이 바뀐다는 내용이에요.

items.title: Less Homework, More Thinking
items.text: Last term, my teacher tried something new. Instead of one hour of homework every night, she gave us twenty minutes of focused practice. I was doubtful at first. How could so little work make any difference? Yet my test scores went up, and I felt less tired in class. I now think the real problem was never the amount of time but the quality of the work. Long assignments often become copying exercises, while short ones push us to think carefully. Of course, some subjects, such as writing, may need more time. Still, I believe schools should ask whether every extra page really helps students learn. Perhaps less homework is not lazy at all. It may simply be smarter.

qs.q: What did the teacher change last term?
o: She stopped giving tests to the whole class.
She added a new writing subject each week.
She taught longer lessons after school.
She shortened the nightly homework.
qs.why: one hour of homework 대신 twenty minutes of focused practice를 주었어요.

qs.q: Which is most likely true about the writer's earlier long homework?
o: It was always too difficult for the writer to finish.
Some of it was done without much thought.
It was never checked by the teacher afterward.
It taught the writer how to write much better.
qs.why: Long assignments often become copying exercises라고 했으므로 생각 없이 베끼는 경우가 있었음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention that writing may need more time?
o: To admit that the idea has limits
To show that the teacher was wrong
To suggest adding more homework
To complain about writing classes
qs.why: Of course, some subjects ... may need more time은 자신의 주장에도 예외가 있다고 인정하는 말이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "focused" is closest in meaning to
o: done with other people
easy and quick
paying full attention to one task
chosen by the students
qs.why: focused practice는 한 가지에 집중하는 연습을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does the writer mainly argue?
o: Homework should be given only in the subject of writing.
Students should never have to take any tests.
The quality of homework matters more than its length.
Teachers should give much more time for each task.
qs.why: the real problem was never the amount of time but the quality라고 주장해요.

items.title: The Wrong Bus
items.text: Haru was already late for his piano lesson when he jumped onto bus 14. Only after five stops did he notice that the bus was heading away from the music school. His face turned hot. He got off at an unfamiliar corner and reached for his phone, but the battery was dead. Then he heard a soft melody drifting from a small shop. Through the window, he saw an old man tuning a piano. Haru hesitated, and then he stepped inside and explained his problem. The man smiled, let him call his teacher from the shop phone, and even asked him to play a short song while he waited. When Haru finished, the man clapped. "Being lost is not always bad," he said. Haru laughed. It was the best lesson of his week.

qs.q: Why could Haru not use his phone?
o: He had left it on the bus.
It was broken by a fall.
The signal was too weak.
Its battery had run out.
qs.why: reached for his phone, but the battery was dead라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why did Haru's face turn hot?
o: He was angry at the driver for a wrong turn.
He felt embarrassed about his mistake.
He was sick from the long and bumpy ride.
He was excited about finding a shop nearby.
qs.why: 틀린 버스를 탄 것을 알고 부끄러워서 얼굴이 달아오른 거예요.

qs.q: What does the man's remark "Being lost is not always bad" suggest?
o: People should always carry a paper map with them.
Piano lessons are not really very important.
Unplanned events can lead to good things.
Buses are a poor way to travel in a city.
qs.why: 길을 잃은 덕분에 좋은 만남이 생겼다는 뜻으로, 뜻밖의 일이 좋은 결과로 이어질 수 있음을 말해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "hesitated" means
o: paused because he was unsure
ran away from a problem quickly
spoke to someone very loudly
waited for a friend to arrive
qs.why: hesitate는 확신이 없어 잠시 망설이는 것을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does "It" in the last sentence refer to?
o: The piano class he missed
The visit to the shop
The bus ride on route 14
The walk to the bus stop
qs.why: 마지막 문장의 It은 가게에서 보낸 시간, 즉 가게를 방문한 일을 가리켜요.

items.title: A Note to the Neighbor
items.text: Dear Mrs. Alvarez, I am the new tenant in apartment 4B, and I wanted to introduce myself properly. I also owe you an apology. Last Tuesday, I practiced my drums until ten o'clock at night, and I realized later that the sound must have traveled through the floor. I should have asked you first. From now on, I will play only between four and seven in the afternoon, and I have bought a rubber pad that makes the drums much quieter. If the sound still disturbs you, please knock on my door. I would much prefer a short conversation to a long silence. I have also baked some bread, which I left outside your door. I hope we can be good neighbors. Sincerely, Jun

qs.q: When does Jun plan to play the drums from now on?
o: In the late afternoon
Before breakfast
Around ten at night
Only on weekends
qs.why: I will play only between four and seven in the afternoon이라고 했어요.

qs.q: What does Jun probably think about the noise problem?
o: It cannot be solved at all by anyone in the building.
It can be solved if the neighbor speaks up.
It was caused by the building and not by Jun.
It was not noticed by anyone in the apartments.
qs.why: If the sound still disturbs you, please knock on my door라고 하므로 이웃이 말해 주면 해결할 수 있다고 생각해요.

qs.q: How does Jun's letter sound?
o: Angry and demanding toward a neighbor
Funny and careless about the noise
Polite and considerate
Cold and formal like a business letter
qs.why: 사과하고 해결책을 제시하며 이웃을 배려하는 공손한 어조예요.

qs.q: In the passage, "disturbs" is closest in meaning to
o: teaches
bothers
pleases
follows
qs.why: disturb는 방해하거나 거슬리게 하다라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the letter mainly about?
o: A request to borrow some bread from a neighbor
An invitation to a drum concert in the building
A complaint about loud music coming from upstairs
An apology and a plan to be a better neighbor
qs.why: 소음에 대해 사과하고 앞으로 연주 시간을 지키겠다는 계획을 알리는 편지예요.

items.title: Gardens in the Sky
items.text: In many crowded cities, there is little room for parks, so some builders have started to look upward. Rooftop gardens turn flat, empty roofs into green spaces filled with grass, herbs, and even small trees. These gardens do more than look pretty. In summer, plants keep the building underneath cooler, which means less electricity is needed for air conditioning. They also catch rainwater, so fewer puddles and floods form in the streets below. Some rooftops grow vegetables that nearby restaurants use the same day. However, building one is not cheap. The roof must be strong enough to hold soil and water, and someone must look after the plants all year. Even so, many city planners argue that the long-term benefits are worth the cost.

qs.q: How do rooftop gardens help a building in summer?
o: They keep the inside cooler.
They block the sunlight completely.
They make the roof stronger.
They bring in more fresh air.
qs.why: plants keep the building underneath cooler라고 했어요.

qs.q: What do city planners probably think about rooftop gardens?
o: They are only a passing fashion that will end soon.
The spending will pay off over time.
They should replace all of the parks in a city.
They are too costly to be useful to anyone.
qs.why: Even so, ... the long-term benefits are worth the cost라고 했으므로 시간이 지나면 비용이 보상된다고 봐요.

qs.q: How does the writer treat the topic?
o: Strongly against the whole idea of rooftop gardens
Amused by the idea, but not taking it seriously
Unsure that gardens can grow on roofs at all
Balanced, mentioning both benefits and costs
qs.why: 장점을 설명한 뒤 However로 비용 문제도 함께 언급해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "argue" is closest in meaning to
o: say with reasons
fight angrily
ask politely
forget easily
qs.why: 여기서 argue는 이유를 들어 주장한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to grow herbs and vegetables in a small home
The advantages and costs of gardens on roofs
Why cities have too little electricity in summer
The long history of public parks in big cities
qs.why: 옥상 정원의 장점과 비용을 함께 설명하는 글이에요.

items.title: The Borrowed Umbrella
items.text: It was pouring when Sora left the library, and she had no umbrella. She stood under the entrance roof, watching the rain, until a boy from her class held out a big blue one. "Take it," he said. "I live two minutes away." Sora wanted to refuse, but she was already late, so she thanked him and ran home. The next morning, she noticed that one of its metal ribs had snapped in the wind. She felt awful. All day she worried about how to tell him. After school, she handed it back with both hands. "I broke it," she said. "I will buy you a new one." He shrugged. "That umbrella has broken five times. My father fixes it every time. Come over and watch, if you like."

qs.q: What was wrong with the umbrella the next morning?
o: The color had faded.
A metal part had snapped.
The handle had come off.
The cloth had a large hole.
qs.why: one of its metal ribs had snapped라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why did Sora hand the umbrella back with both hands?
o: Because it was very heavy
Because her arms were tired
To keep it from getting wet
To show respect and regret
qs.why: 두 손으로 건네는 행동은 미안함과 예의를 나타내요.

qs.q: What does the boy's reply show about him?
o: He is careless with his things and never repairs them.
He wants Sora to pay him back as soon as she can.
He is angry about it but tries to hide his feelings.
He is relaxed about small accidents.
qs.why: That umbrella has broken five times ... 라고 느긋하게 답해서 작은 사고에 개의치 않음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "snapped" is closest in meaning to
o: bent slowly
shone brightly
broke suddenly
opened wide
qs.why: snap은 갑자기 부러지다라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What happens at the turning point of the story?
o: Sora decides to keep the umbrella.
Sora learns the boy is not upset.
The rain stops at last.
The boy asks for a new umbrella.
qs.why: Sora가 사과하자 소년이 화내지 않고 대수롭지 않게 반응하면서 이야기의 분위기가 바뀌어요.

items.title: Stargazing Night
items.text: Join us for Stargazing Night at Pine Hill Park on Friday, November 13! The sky forecast is clear, so volunteers from the local astronomy club will set up six telescopes near the east gate, starting at 7:30 p.m. Beginners are very welcome. Members will show you how to find the Moon's craters, a bright planet, and a famous star cluster, and they will answer any questions. Admission is free, but because the telescopes are shared, each person will have about two minutes at the eyepiece. Please dress warmly, since it can get cold on the hill after dark, and bring a flashlight covered with red paper so that other people's eyes can stay used to the dark. If clouds roll in, the event will move to the following Friday.

qs.q: Why should visitors cover their flashlights with red paper?
o: So the light can reach much farther across the hill
So the batteries inside the lights last longer
So other people's eyes can adjust to the dark
So the telescopes stay clean during the night
qs.why: red paper는 other people's eyes can stay used to the dark를 위한 거예요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the event?
o: Only club members may look through the telescopes at all.
Telescopes are too expensive for people to share.
The park is already crowded on every Friday night.
Many visitors are expected to use the telescopes.
qs.why: 각자 two minutes만 볼 수 있다는 것은 망원경을 쓰려는 사람이 많을 것임을 암시해요.

qs.q: What is the tone of the announcement?
o: Strict and serious
Welcoming and encouraging
Sad and tired
Surprised and angry
qs.why: Beginners are very welcome처럼 참가를 반기고 권하는 어조예요.

qs.q: In the passage, "admission" means
o: a mistake
an opinion
a seat in a car
the right to enter
qs.why: admission은 입장(료)을 뜻해요. 무료라는 문맥과 맞아요.

qs.q: Who does "they" in "they will answer any questions" refer to?
o: The beginners
The members
The telescopes
The visitors
qs.why: 앞 문장의 주어 Members가 질문에 답한다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: The Last Day of the Shoe Shop
items.text: Mr. Han had repaired shoes at the same small shop for forty years. When the rent doubled, he decided to close. On the last day, he hung a sign in the window: "Thank you, and goodbye." He expected a quiet afternoon. Instead, the door kept opening. A woman brought in boots her mother had worn. A teenager arrived with sneakers worn through at the toes. A child came with a drawing of the shop. By closing time, the shelves held more gifts than shoes: flowers, cards, and a cake. Mr. Han looked around slowly. He had always thought of himself as someone people only visited when something was broken. Now he understood he had been part of the neighborhood all along. He locked the door, but this time he was smiling.

qs.q: Why did Mr. Han decide to close the shop?
o: He wanted to retire to the countryside.
The rent became too high.
Customers had stopped coming.
His tools had worn out.
qs.why: When the rent doubled, he decided to close라고 했어요.

qs.q: What did Mr. Han believe before the last day?
o: His shop was the best repair shop in the whole town.
Children in the neighborhood did not like his shop.
Nobody in the neighborhood would miss him at all.
People valued him only for fixing things.
qs.why: someone people only visited when something was broken이라고 생각했어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer list flowers, cards, and a cake?
o: To explain all of the things that the shop sold
To describe a birthday party held in the shop
To show that the shelves were broken and needed repair
To show how much people appreciated him
qs.why: 선물들은 사람들이 그에게 고마워했음을 보여 줘요.

qs.q: In the passage, "all along" means
o: for a short moment
over a long distance
the whole time
together with others
qs.why: all along은 '처음부터 내내'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How does Mr. Han change by the end of the story?
o: He decides to move to another city and start again.
He becomes angry at his customers for coming late.
He plans to open a bigger shop in a better place.
He sees his place in the community differently.
qs.why: 자신이 동네의 일부였다는 것을 깨닫고 미소를 지어요.

items.title: Let Children Cook
items.text: Many parents think the kitchen is no place for children, with its hot stoves and sharp knives. I disagree. When I was nine, my uncle taught me to make fried rice, starting with washing the vegetables and measuring the rice. He stayed next to me the whole time. Within a month, I could cook a simple meal by myself. The benefits went beyond food. I learned to read instructions carefully, manage my time, and clean up afterward. Best of all, I became curious about ingredients I once refused to eat. Of course, young cooks need supervision and clear safety rules. But protecting children from every risk also keeps them from learning useful skills. I say we hand them an apron instead of a worry.

qs.q: What did the writer's uncle do while teaching?
o: He cooked all the meals himself.
He left to answer the phone.
He stayed beside the writer.
He gave written tests.
qs.why: He stayed next to me the whole time이라고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the writer as a young child?
o: The writer cooked a full meal every day at that age.
The writer disliked all the members of the family.
The writer did not eat some foods.
The writer was afraid of using any kitchen knives.
qs.why: ingredients I once refused to eat에서 가리는 음식이 있었음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer tell the story about the uncle?
o: To show that cooking can be safe with guidance
To praise the uncle's restaurant to the readers
To explain exactly how to wash vegetables properly
To prove that rice is healthier than other foods
qs.why: 삼촌이 곁에서 지켜보며 가르쳐 준 경험으로 안전하게 요리를 배울 수 있음을 보여 줘요.

qs.q: In the passage, "supervision" is closest in meaning to
o: trying new recipes
watching over by an adult
buying fresh food
cleaning the kitchen
qs.why: supervision은 어른이 지켜보며 돌보는 것을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does the writer mainly argue?
o: Children should learn to cook with adult help.
Children should cook alone every night of the week.
Kitchens should be closed to all young children.
Parents should stop eating meals at home.
qs.why: young cooks need supervision이라고 하면서 아이들이 요리를 배워야 한다고 주장해요.

items.title: Losing the Queen
items.text: Dae-ho had never lost to anyone in his school's chess club, so when a new student named Elena joined, he agreed to play her without much thought. Within ten moves, he knew he was in trouble. Elena moved quietly, never smiling, and he began to sweat. Finally, he made a mistake and lost his queen. Dae-ho wanted to push the board off the table. Instead he took a breath and asked, "How did you plan that last move?" Elena looked surprised, and then she began to explain, drawing little diagrams on a napkin. An hour later, the two were still talking, and the board lay forgotten. "Can we play again tomorrow?" Dae-ho asked. For the first time, he did not care who would win.

qs.q: How did Dae-ho lose the game?
o: He lost his queen after a mistake.
He ran out of time before the last move.
He forgot some of the rules of chess.
He was asked by Elena to stop playing.
qs.why: he made a mistake and lost his queen이라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why did Elena look surprised?
o: She had never played a game of chess before then.
She had not expected a question instead of anger.
She thought that the game had ended in a draw.
She did not know the name of her opponent.
qs.why: 패배 직후 화를 낼 줄 알았던 Dae-ho가 질문을 해서 놀란 거예요.

qs.q: What is the turning point of the story?
o: Elena joins the chess club at the start of the term.
Dae-ho pushes the board off the table in anger.
The two players stop talking and leave the room.
Dae-ho asks a question instead of getting upset.
qs.why: 분위기가 바뀌는 순간은 Dae-ho가 화내는 대신 질문하는 때예요.

qs.q: In the passage, "diagrams" are
o: notes written to a teacher
simple drawings that explain something
pieces used in the game
rules printed on paper
qs.why: diagram은 설명을 돕는 간단한 그림이나 도표예요.

qs.q: What does the last sentence suggest about Dae-ho?
o: He wants to leave the club and never play again.
He plans to beat Elena as soon as he can.
He is tired of playing chess with new players.
He now values learning more than winning.
qs.why: For the first time, he did not care who would win은 이기는 것보다 배우는 것을 중요하게 여기게 되었음을 보여 줘요.

items.title: Across the Pool
items.text: Dear Grandpa, Guess what? I swam a whole length of the pool yesterday without touching the bottom! You may remember that I was afraid of deep water. Every time my coach asked me to let go of the wall, my legs began to shake. Then she suggested something odd: counting my kicks out loud. I felt silly at first, but the numbers kept my mind busy, and soon I forgot to be scared. By the twentieth kick, I was across. My coach cheered so loudly that people at the other end of the pool turned to look. I wish you could have seen my face. Next month, there is a small race for beginners. I haven't decided to join, but I'm thinking about it. Love, Minseo

qs.q: What helped Minseo get across the pool?
o: Holding on to the wall of the pool
Swimming together with a friend
Counting kicks out loud
Wearing a brand-new swimsuit
qs.why: counting my kicks out loud로 마음을 다른 곳에 돌려 두려움을 잊었어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Grandpa?
o: He is also a swimming coach.
He is afraid of deep water.
He will join the race.
He did not see the swim.
qs.why: I wish you could have seen my face는 할아버지가 그 자리에 없었음을 뜻해요.

qs.q: How does Minseo feel in the letter?
o: Bored with swimming lessons and wanting to stop
Angry at the coach for cheering too loudly
Worried about the depth of the pool
Proud, but not fully sure about the race
qs.why: 성공을 자랑스러워하지만 I haven't decided to join이라며 대회는 망설여요.

qs.q: In the passage, "odd" is closest in meaning to
o: famous
quiet
strange
helpful
qs.why: odd는 '이상한, 특이한'이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the letter mainly about?
o: Overcoming a fear with a simple trick
Planning a long trip to visit Grandpa
Choosing the best swimming school in town
Winning a race for beginners next month
qs.why: 깊은 물에 대한 두려움을 킥 숫자를 세는 방법으로 이겨 낸 이야기예요.

items.title: Why Do We Yawn?
items.text: Everyone yawns, yet scientists still cannot fully explain why. For years, people believed yawning brings extra oxygen to a tired body. However, experiments have not supported this idea: people who breathed extra oxygen still yawned just as often. A newer theory suggests that yawning helps cool the brain. A deep breath pulls cooler air into the head, which may help us stay alert when we feel sleepy. Another curious fact is that yawns are contagious. Merely seeing or reading about a yawn can make you want to do the same, and even dogs sometimes yawn after their owners do. Researchers think this may be connected to feeling close to others. So the next time you yawn in class, do not blame your teacher too quickly. It might be your brain asking for a little cooling.

qs.q: What did the experiments show about extra oxygen?
o: It made people yawn much less often.
It did not reduce how often people yawned.
It made people feel very sleepy at once.
It cooled the brain more quickly than air.
qs.why: people who breathed extra oxygen still yawned just as often라고 했어요.

qs.q: What does the passage suggest about the cooling theory?
o: It has been proved by every experiment so far.
It was believed by most people for many years.
It is a possible explanation, not a proven fact.
It is the oldest theory about yawning of all.
qs.why: A newer theory suggests ... may help라는 표현으로 아직 증명되지 않은 가설임을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What is the tone of the last two sentences?
o: Serious and worried
Harsh and critical
Sad and quiet
Light and playful
qs.why: 선생님을 탓하지 말라는 농담 섞인 말투로 글을 마무리해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "contagious" describes something that
o: happens only at night
spreads from one to another
is very hard to see
lasts for a short time
qs.why: contagious는 하품이 다른 사람에게 옮는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to stop yourself from yawning in class
Why dogs and their owners look alike
The best way to get a good night's sleep
Theories about why people yawn
qs.why: 하품의 이유에 대한 여러 이론을 소개하는 글이에요.

items.title: Swap Shop Sunday
items.text: Is your closet full of clothes you never wear? Bring them to the Maple Street Swap Shop on Sunday, March 8, from noon until 3:00 p.m. Here is how it works. At the door, volunteers will count the items you bring and give you one ticket for each. Then you can browse the tables and trade your tickets for anything you like. Everything must be clean and in good condition, with no holes or missing buttons. Shoes, coats, and children's clothes are especially needed this year. At the end of the day, anything left over will be given to the Hope Clothing Center. You do not have to bring items to take part: first-timers receive three free tickets. Our goal is simple: keep good clothes out of the trash and save everyone money.

qs.q: How do visitors get tickets?
o: They get one for each item they bring.
They buy them from the volunteers at the door.
They win them by playing a game at the tables.
They get one for each hour that they stay.
qs.why: volunteers will count the items you bring and give you one ticket for each라고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about a first-time visitor with no clothes to bring?
o: The visitor must leave the shop without any clothes.
The visitor must pay money for each piece of clothing.
The visitor can only help the volunteers all day.
The visitor can still take some clothes home.
qs.why: first-timers receive three free tickets이므로 빈손이어도 옷을 가져갈 수 있어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer begin with a question?
o: To test what readers already know
To introduce the volunteers
To make readers think about their own unused clothes
To complain about messy closets
qs.why: 옷장에 안 입는 옷이 가득하냐는 질문으로 독자가 자신의 상황을 떠올리게 해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "browse" means
o: look through things casually
carry heavy items
count one by one
clean carefully
qs.why: browse는 가볍게 훑어보다라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A sale of brand-new shoes and winter coats
A tour of a large clothing factory
An event where people trade used clothes
A class on how to sew on missing buttons
qs.why: 안 입는 옷을 가져와 다른 옷과 교환하는 행사를 안내하는 글이에요.

items.title: The Late Package
items.text: A package arrived at Yuna's door, addressed to "Mr. R. Park, 12B." Yuna lived in 12A. She almost put it in the recycling bin, but the label said "Fragile." She carried it down the hall and knocked. An elderly man opened the door slowly. "Oh," he said, "this must be the music box for my wife's birthday. I thought it was lost." Yuna felt pleased until he added that the party had been the previous week. The birthday had passed, and the box had arrived late. Yuna's heart sank. But the man smiled. "She will not mind," he said. "She always says that a late gift shows you were thinking of someone for longer." Then he invited Yuna in for tea.

qs.q: What stopped Yuna from throwing the package away?
o: The sound of Mr. Park's loud knock on the door
The word "Fragile" on the label
A note from the postman asking her to deliver it
The heavy weight of the box in her arms
qs.why: the label said "Fragile"이라서 버리지 않았어요.

qs.q: Why did Yuna's heart sink?
o: She realized the gift had come too late.
She dropped the music box in the hallway.
She could not find the door of apartment 12B.
She was not invited to the party at all.
qs.why: The birthday had passed, and the box had arrived late라서 실망한 거예요.

qs.q: How does Mr. Park react to the late gift?
o: He is gracious and understanding.
He is upset and impatient about the delay.
He is surprised and suspicious of Yuna.
He is bored and uninterested in the gift.
qs.why: She will not mind라며 웃고 차를 대접하는 너그러운 태도예요.

qs.q: In the passage, "elderly" is closest in meaning to
o: very tall
quite rich
rather old
slightly sick
qs.why: elderly는 '나이가 지긋한'이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Who does "She" in "She will not mind" refer to?
o: Yuna
Mr. Park's wife
A delivery worker
The neighbor in 12A
qs.why: 앞서 언급된 my wife's birthday의 wife, 즉 Mr. Park의 아내를 가리켜요.
